03 / STRUCTURE SELECTED
Thin sheets form upright, open-ended rolls that sit closely together. Repeated hollow openings and short walls create the distinctive clustered structure.
This is a staggered repetition, not a strict radial or graduated pattern. A balanced arrangement makes it clear at small sizes.

Trace the oval rim, curved basket wall and many upright rolls. Keep their open tops, short sides and slightly uneven edges. Omit the sauce bowls, table and surface texture so the packed structure is easier to read.

Keep the hollow noodle rolls; remove the steamer.
Reduce the many rolls to five matching units: three behind and two in front. Use shallow ellipses for the openings and gently tapered sides for the walls. Curved lower edges suggest volume.

Remove construction guides and uneven edges. Keep clear hollow centres and a consistent stroke. The five-roll arrangement is a design choice that preserves the repeated structure while making a compact, balanced icon.
